name: 'Alim
description: Minor Social Status Virtue for members of the Muslim religious elite, such as mu'adhdhin, imam, mufti or qadi; allows purchase of Academic Abilities and is male-only.

name: Bureaucrat
description: Minor Social Status Virtue for a member of the Muslim civil administration, such as a katib or watha'iqi; allows Academic Abilities.

name: Educated (Islamic)
description: Minor General Virtue for characters educated in a mosque or Qur'an school, granting 50 experience points in Arabic, Persian, Greek, Latin, Theology: Islam, Islamic Law and Artes Liberales.

name: Emir
description: Minor Social Status Virtue equivalent to Knight for Muslim nobles, who are also likely skilled in hunting, religious teaching and culture.

name: Mamluk
description: Minor Social Status Virtue for a former military slave trained at a military school, educated in Islam and freed at adulthood; grants Martial Abilities and Theology: Islam.

name: Muqta'
description: Major Social Status Virtue for an important emir entrusted with an iqta' (a fief); follows the Landed Noble rules.

name: Sufi
description: Minor Social Status or Supernatural Virtue for a Muslim mystic belonging to a Sufi tariqa led by a shaykh; includes the Mentor Flaw and access to Theology: Islam, Islamic Law and Dominion Lore.

name: Dhimmi
description: Minor General Flaw for a non-Muslim living under Muslim rule who must pay the jizya head tax and abide by social restrictions in return for protection.

name: Eunuch
description: Minor General Flaw for a castrated male character, often made so for work in a harem or military school; grants freedom of movement among the sexes.

name: Outsider
description: Social Status Flaw (Major, with a new Minor version for grogs) representing hostility faced by Muslims in non-Muslim lands and required of all Jewish characters.

name: Magister in Artibus
description: Major Social Status Virtue forbidden to Muslim and Jewish characters, since European-style universities are unavailable to them.

name: Clerk
description: Minor Social Status Virtue forbidden to Muslim characters.

name: Mendicant Friar
description: Minor Social Status Virtue forbidden to Muslim characters.

name: Priest
description: Minor Social Status Virtue forbidden to Muslim characters.

name: Monastic Vows
description: Major Story Flaw forbidden to Muslim and Jewish characters.

name: Branded Criminal
description: Minor Social Status Flaw forbidden to Muslim characters because criminals are not branded in Muslim societies.

name: Knight
description: Social Status Virtue implying a feudal position; the Emir Virtue mirrors it, and it is forbidden to Jewish characters.

name: Landed Noble
description: Social Status Virtue whose rules apply to the Muqta'; forbidden to Jewish characters.

name: Warrior
description: Minor General Virtue forbidden to Jewish characters because of restrictions on carrying arms and armor.

name: Mentor
description: Minor Story Flaw automatically possessed by Sufis, representing their shaykh.

name: True Faith
description: Virtue required of all zahids.

name: Meditation
description: Holy Method Ability favored by Sufis, required for zahids; Dream Interpretation and Gematria can substitute for it.

name: Understanding
description: Holy Power Ability favored by Sufis and required of zahids.

name: Second Sight
description: Supernatural Ability required of zahids.

name: Ceremony
description: Ability enabling a leader such as a Sufi shaykh to synchronize the efforts of group ritual participants.

name: Transcendence
description: Holy Power favored by Sufis.

name: Invocation
description: Holy Method favored by Zoroastrian magi and Ba'al Shem; associated with the Zoroastrian rituals.

name: Holy Magic
description: Virtue required to cast the Zoroastrian holy rituals and favored by the Zoroastrian societas.

name: Sense Holiness and Unholiness
description: Supernatural Ability favored by Zoroastrian magi and possessed by the devout mu'adhdhin.

name: Wonders
description: Holy Power favored by Zoroastrians and associated with their holy rituals.

name: Wise One
description: Minor Social Status Virtue a zahid may take when living in Muslim lands.

name: Dependent
description: Major Story Flaw taken by a zahid shaykh to represent his Sufi tariqa.

name: Zahid
description: Free Mythic Companion Virtue that all zahids must begin with.

name: Zahids
description: Mythic Companions who are exceptionally ascetic Sufis, often shaykhs, able to work miraculous karamas and synchronize followers' efforts.

name: Islamic Law
description: Academic Ability, the Muslim version of Civil & Canon Law, drawn from the Qur'an and Sunna.

name: Theology: Islam
description: Academic Ability, the Islamic equivalent of Christian Theology, based on the Qur'an and Sunna.

name: Dominion Lore
description: Arcane Ability purchasable by Sufis and required of zahids.

name: Holy Tradition: Sufis
description: Holy tradition of Muslim mystics who gather in tariqas to seek God through communal dhikr and sama' meditation, led by a shaykh.

name: Tariqa
description: A Sufi group or order led by a shaykh, gathering for communal meditation rituals.

name: Shaykh
description: Holy leader of a Sufi tariqa, often possessing the Ceremony Ability.

name: Dhikr
description: Sufi group meditation in which the names of God are intoned with bodily movement until closeness with Him is achieved.

name: Sama'
description: Sufi group meditation of listening to music or poetry composed for God to reach an ecstatic state.

name: Karamas
description: Miraculous acts worked by zahids through pious contemplation.

name: Holy Societas: Zoroastrians
description: Ancient holy tradition founded by Zoroaster; by 1220 a new generation in the Levant and Thebes, with Gifted members mostly in House Flambeau.

name: Zoroaster
description: Prophet who founded the Persian faith on monotheism and revealed the Gathas.

name: Gathas
description: Divine hymns of Zoroaster revealing Ahura Mazda.

name: Ahura Mazda
description: The one supreme, all-knowing God of Zoroastrianism, the 'Wise Lord'.

name: Angra Mainyu
description: The 'Destructive Spirit', opposite of Ahura Mazda, bringing disorder, falsehood and suffering.

name: Amesha Spentas
description: The 'Beneficent Immortals' personifying the seven pillars of the material world.

name: Magoi
description: Zoroastrian priests who venerate fire, pursue truth and fight servants of Angra Mainyu; source of the word 'magus'.

name: House Flambeau
description: Hermetic House to which most Zoroastrian magi belong, owing to veneration of fire and fighting evil.

name: Order of Hermes
description: The Hermetic order which several Gifted Zoroastrian refugees joined.

name: The Gift
description: Magical aptitude possessed by some Zoroastrian refugees who joined the Order of Hermes.

name: (Immortal)'s Blessing
description: CrVi(Gen) Zoroastrian holy ritual granting a casting bonus to a following spell of a Form associated with one of seven Immortals, limited by a Personality trait.

name: Asha Vahishta
description: One of the Zoroastrian Immortals (Amesha Spentas): 'Best Righteousness', associated with Brave and Ignem/Imaginem in the Blessing ritual.

name: Khshathra Vairya
description: One of the Zoroastrian Immortals (Amesha Spentas): 'Desirable Dominion', associated with Just and Vim in the Blessing ritual.

name: Haurvatat
description: One of the Zoroastrian Immortals (Amesha Spentas): 'Health', associated with Strong and Aquam/Auram in the Blessing ritual.

name: Spenta Armaiti
description: One of the Zoroastrian Immortals (Amesha Spentas): 'Holy Devotion', associated with Loyal and Terram in the Blessing ritual.

name: Ameretat
description: One of the Zoroastrian Immortals (Amesha Spentas): 'Long Life', associated with Calm and Herbam in the Blessing ritual.

name: Vohu Manah
description: One of the Zoroastrian Immortals (Amesha Spentas): 'Good Purpose', associated with Kind and Animal in the Blessing ritual.

name: Spenta Mainyu
description: One of the Zoroastrian Immortals (Amesha Spentas): 'Holy Spirit', associated with Wise and Corpus/Mentem in the Blessing ritual.

name: Saoshyant's Elixir
description: CrCo50 Zoroastrian ritual requiring ordeal by molten metal and sacrifice of a holy bull; the drinker need not make aging rolls and cannot die while following Zoroastrianism, gaining Warping instead.

name: Saoshyant
description: The Savior, Seed of Zoroaster, from whom the elixir of eternal life was handed down.

name: Longevity Ritual
description: Hermetic ritual that loses effectiveness when Saoshyant's Elixir is performed.

name: Warping
description: Points gained yearly by those under Saoshyant's Elixir.

name: Final Twilight
description: Zoroastrians believe those entering Final Twilight after the elixir join Ahura Mazda in Paradise.

name: The Mysteries (Revised)
description: Forthcoming book said to cover initiation into Holy Magic.

name: Mu'adhdhin
description: Mosque attendant who summons the faithful to prayer; basis of the Devout Mu'adhdhin grog template.

name: Katib
description: Scribe or secretary of the Muslim bureaucracy; basis of the Christian Katib grog template.

name: Qadi
description: Muslim judge; basis of the High-Ranking Qadi companion template.

name: Mufti
description: Someone formally entitled to give a legal opinion in Islam.

name: The Mamluk Soldier
description: Grog template for a low-ranking Turkish Mamluk soldier.

name: The Mamluk Emir
description: Companion template for a proud, reckless, land-holding Mamluk noble cursed by jinn.

name: The Muslim Traveller
description: Companion template for a Muslim scholar wandering Europe, inspired by a guardian angel.

name: The Sufi Poetess
description: Companion template for a blind Sufi poetess, a living saint able to heal with a touch.

name: Iqta'
description: Muslim land grant similar to a feudal fief entrusted to a muqta'.

name: Jizya
description: Head tax paid by adult male dhimmis.

name: Student of Divine
description: Virtue granting a bonus to Dominion Lore, held by the Sufi Poetess.

name: Lesser Purifying Touch
description: Virtue letting the Sufi Poetess heal (Quotidian Fever) with a touch.

name: Guardian Angel
description: Virtue of the Muslim Traveller, whose angel inspires him to explore holy sites.

name: Lesser Malediction
description: Flaw of the Mamluk Emir, cursed by jinn to wound a companion in every battle.

name: Jinn
description: Spirits who cursed the Mamluk Emir.

name: Jewish People
description: Exiled worshipers of the one God, dispersed across Mythic Europe and the East in the diaspora, often persecuted.

name: Abraham
description: Father of the Jewish people who covenanted with God; credited as author of the Sefer Yetzirah.

name: Jacob
description: Abraham's grandson, father of twelve sons.

name: Joseph
description: Son of Jacob sold into slavery in Egypt who gained Pharaoh's favor through Divine prophecies.

name: Moses
description: Prophet who freed the Hebrews from Egypt and received the Ten Commandments and Torah at Sinai.

name: Joshua
description: Conqueror of Canaan.

name: Bezalel
description: Craftsman who built the Ark, with profound understanding of creation through Hebrew letters.

name: Ark of the Covenant
description: Ark built by Bezalel holding the tablets of the Ten Commandments, Aaron's rod and manna.

name: Ten Commandments
description: Stone tablets received by Moses at Sinai.

name: Saul
description: First king of Israel.

name: David
description: King of Israel; the Star of David is said to resemble his shield.

name: Solomon
description: King of great wisdom and magical power who built the Temple in Jerusalem; knew the location of Luz from birds.

name: Rehoboam
description: Solomon's son under whom Israel split into Israel and Judah.

name: Nebuchadnezzar
description: Conqueror of Jerusalem in 587 BC who destroyed the First Temple.

name: Cyrus the Great
description: Persian king who returned the Jews to Israel in 539 BC.

name: Temple in Jerusalem
description: The Temple built by Solomon, destroyed in 587 BC, rebuilt as the Second Temple and destroyed by the Romans.

name: Western Wall
description: All that remains of the Temple, with a Divine aura of 10.

name: Jerusalem
description: Capital of Judah and site of the Temple, holier than the rest of Israel.

name: Israel
description: Jewish homeland, formerly Canaan, considered holy.

name: Judah
description: Southern kingdom with Jerusalem as capital.

name: Canaan
description: Land promised to Abraham, which became Israel.

name: Babylon
description: Place of Jewish exile; its great yeshivot are the pinnacle of Jewish scholarship.

name: Mount Sinai
description: Where Moses received the Torah from God.

name: Egypt
description: Land where the Hebrews were enslaved.

name: Diaspora
description: The dispersal of the Jews after the fall of the Second Temple.

name: Ashkenazim
description: Jews in Christian lands, mostly France and Germany, socially isolated and turned towards theology and mysticism.

name: Sephardim
description: Jews of Muslim and Mediterranean lands who embrace secular learning and public life.

name: Karaites
description: Small Jewish sect founded in Persia basing theology on the Tanakh alone and rejecting the Talmud.

name: Rabbinical Judaism
description: Majority Jewish sect grounded in interpretation of Tanakh and Talmud.

name: Kabbalah
description: Jewish mysticism seeking to manifest Divine principles; also a Major Supernatural Virtue and Ability usable as Invocation and enabling golem creation.

name: Almohads
description: Muslim power whose push into Andalusia displaces Sephardic communities.

name: Andalusia
description: Region from which Sephardim are being displaced.

name: Provence
description: Region with the strongest Kabbalah adherents.

name: Constantinople
description: City where Jewish and Karaite quarters are divided by a gateless wall; its Jewish community suffered in 1204.

name: Byzantine Empire
description: Empire tolerating Jews under restrictions.

name: Baghdad
description: City home to the Exilarch.

name: Exilarch
description: Notional head of all diaspora Jews, based in Baghdad, able to extend Holy Influence.

name: Fourth Lateran Council
description: Council of 1215 requiring Jews to wear distinguishing marks.

name: Innocent III
description: Pope who clarified the Lateran legislation and cancelled crusaders' debts in 1215.

name: Bishop of Speyer
description: Bishop who sheltered Jews from a mob in his castle in 1096.

name: Worms
description: City whose Jews found no protector in 1096.

name: Norwich
description: English city whose Jews were massacred in 1190 and site of the first blood libel.

name: York
description: English city where besieged Jews in the castle took their own lives in 1190.

name: Ba'al Ov
description: Necromantic practitioners of summoning magic outlawed by Halakha.

name: Ba'al Shem
description: Itinerant practitioners of Divine magic specializing in folk healing and seggulot; also a Free Social Status Virtue and holy tradition.

name: Beth Din
description: Rabbinic court hearing cases under halakhic law, led by the Rosh Beth Din.

name: Beit ha-midrash
description: School attached to a synagogue focused on Hebrew literacy.

name: Gematria
description: School of Jewish mysticism using numerology of Hebrew letters; Major Supernatural Virtue and Ability usable in place of Meditation.

name: Golem
description: Being of unliving clay brought to life by a kabbalist through Divine forces.

name: Halakha
description: Jewish law as laid down in the Torah and interpreted by rabbis.

name: Kashrut
description: Dietary requirements codified in the Torah; kosher food complies.

name: Merkavah
description: School of Jewish mysticism communing with angels via True Names; Major Supernatural Virtue usable in place of Purity.

name: Miqveh
description: Communal ritual bathhouse maintaining halakhic purity.

name: Mitzvot
description: The 613 lawful deeds dictated by the Torah.

name: Rabbi
description: Religious leader and teacher of a Jewish community; a Minor Social Status Virtue.

name: Sefirot
description: The ten emanations of Divine power forming the Tree of Life in Kabbalah.

name: Seggulot
description: Amulets fusing folk knowledge and Divine magic.

name: Shabbat
description: Day of rest from Friday to Saturday sundown.

name: Shema
description: Statement of Jewish belief from Deuteronomy 6:4, used in tefillin and mezuzot.

name: Shofar
description: Instrument made from a kosher animal's horn; a relic with one Faith Point when sounded on holy days or in exorcism.

name: Synagogue
description: Gathering place for Rabbinical Jews to hear Torah readings.

name: Talmud
description: Book of interpretations of Halakha and cultural wisdom; a Summa on Judaic Lore, Theology: Judaism and Rabbinic Law.

name: Tanakh
description: The Hebrew Bible, comprising Torah, Nevi'im and Ketuvim.

name: Torah
description: First five books of the Tanakh transcribed by Moses; a Summa on Theology: Judaism, Judaic Lore and Rabbinic Law.

name: Sefer Torah
description: Ceremonial scroll of the Torah in a synagogue, treated as a relic with one Faith Point.

name: True Torah
description: Primordial Torah of black fire on white fire residing in heaven.

name: Yeshivah
description: Advanced school where learned rabbis teach.

name: Blood Libel
description: Unfounded accusation that Jews practice human sacrifice.

name: William of Norwich
description: Boy involved in the first blood libel accusation in England in 1144.

name: Philip II of France
description: King who ransomed and expelled Jews in 1182 and recalled them in 1198.

name: Richard
description: English king whose ransom was paid in part by taxing Jews.

name: Maimonides
description: Philosopher and physician (1138-1204) who codified 13 articles of faith and wrote the Mishneh Torah and Guide to the Perplexed.

name: Gehenna
description: Jewish understanding of Hell where souls are cleansed before resurrection.

name: Semikhah
description: Rabbinic ordination granting authority over halakhic law and Dominion auras.

name: Rosh ha-Shanah
description: Jewish new year on 1 Tishri when all are judged.

name: Sefer ha-Chayyim
description: Book of Names in which those meriting another year are recorded.

name: Yom Kippur
description: Day of Atonement closing the Sefer ha-Chayyim.

name: Kapparah
description: Ritual of transferring sins to a chicken before Yom Kippur.

name: Holy Influence
description: Exertion of spiritual authority, including tempering an aura.

name: Presbyter Judaeorum
description: Chief rabbi of all English Jews, held in 1220 by Josce of London.

name: Josce of London
description: Presbyter Judaeorum of England in 1220.

name: Sukkot
description: Harvest festival commemorating forty years in the wilderness.

name: Shemini Atzeret
description: Festival marking the end and beginning of the Torah reading cycle.

name: Hanukkah
description: Eight-day festival commemorating the miracle of oil.

name: Purim
description: Celebration with public reading of the Book of Esther.

name: Pesach
description: Passover commemorating the escape from Egypt.

name: Shavu'ot
description: Festival celebrating revelation at Sinai.

name: Tisha B'Av
description: Fast commemorating destruction of both Temples.

name: Hebrew Calendar
description: Lunar calendar with a 19-year cycle; Julian 1 April 1220 equals 26 Nisan 4980.

name: Judah Halevi
description: Toledo-born poet (1075-1140) who held Israel the only place for true prophecy; murdered outside Jerusalem.

name: Tefillin
description: Leather boxes containing the Shema; those owned by a Tzadik Nistar act as a relic.

name: Mezuzot
description: Phylactery cases bound to door posts.

name: Menorah
description: Six- or eight-branched candelabrum; the eight-branched chanukkiyah is used at Hanukkah.

name: Star of David
description: Six-pointed star symbolizing God with kabbalistic resonance.

name: Nevi'im
description: The Prophets, second section of the Tanakh; Tractatus on Theology: Judaism and Dream Interpretation.

name: Ketuvim
description: The Writings, final section of the Tanakh; a collection of tractatus.

name: Mishneh Torah
description: Maimonides' Summa on Rabbinic Law, the foremost authority.

name: Guide to the Perplexed
description: Maimonides' philosophical work; Summa Philosophiae and Theology: Judaism, and a Gematria tractatus.

name: Sefer Yetzirah
description: Book of Creation attributed to Abraham; Summa Kabbalah required to create a golem.

name: Ma'asei-Bereshit
description: School of philosophy seeking the foundations of creation, based on the Sefer Yetzirah.

name: Sefer ha-Bahir
description: Book of Illumination by Provencal kabbalists; Tractatus on Kabbalah and Ceremony.

name: Sefer ha-Razim
description: Book of Amulets revealed to Noah by Raziel; tractatus on Craft Amulets, Merkavah, Ceremony and Dominion Lore.

name: Raziel
description: Angel who revealed the Sefer ha-Razim to Noah and Sefer Raziel to Adam.

name: Noah
description: Recipient of the Sefer ha-Razim.

name: Adam
description: Recipient of the original Sefer Raziel.

name: Sefer Raziel
description: Book of sorcery on astral forces; Summae on Gematria, Merkavah, Intervention and Transcendence.

name: Hechalot Texts
description: Scrolls on Ma'aseh Merkavah; studying them alone grants 'Curious about the Infernal'.

name: Ma'aseh Merkavah
description: Ancient mystical tradition from which Merkavah and Goetic Summoning derive.

name: Summoning
description: Goetic art deriving from Ma'aseh Merkavah.

name: Sword of Moses
description: Theurgic book naming angels and demons; Summa Infernal Lore and insight into Canaanite Necromancy.

name: Canaanite Necromancy
description: Extinct magical form researchable via the Sword of Moses.

name: Craft Amulets
description: Supernatural Ability to make seggulot; also a Minor Supernatural Virtue.

name: Dream Interpretation
description: Supernatural Ability to divine prophetic dreams, usable in place of Meditation.

name: Rabbinic Law
description: Academic Ability of Jewish law.

name: Theology: Judaism
description: Academic Ability of Jewish theology.

name: Judaic Lore
description: Lore Ability of Jewish folklore and culture.

name: Benjamin of Tudela
description: 12th-century traveler from Navarre to Jerusalem who recorded Jewish communities and wrote the Sefer ha-Masa'ot.

name: Sefer ha-Masa'ot
description: The Book of Travels; Summa Mediterranean Lore.

name: Kingdom of Sicily
description: Kingdom accepting of multiple cultures; Jews held the silk monopoly under Frederick II.

name: Palermo
description: City with fifteen hundred Jews.

name: Chelm
description: Mythical city of fools of Jewish folklore.

name: Nehardea
description: Babylonian yeshivah city.

name: Pumbedita
description: Babylonian yeshivah city.

name: Sura
description: Babylonian yeshivah city where Saadia Gaon was Gaon.

name: Geonim
description: Title of leaders of the Babylonian yeshivot.

name: Isaac Ben Solomon Israeli
description: Tunisian physician (850-932), monist and accomplished kabbalist.

name: Saadia Gaon
description: Gaon of Sura (882-942), opponent of the Karaites.

name: Samuel ben Judah ibn Tibbon
description: Translator of Maimonides living in Marseilles until 1230.

name: Shadchan
description: Marriage arranger; a Minor Social Status Virtue open to men and women.

name: Cherem
description: Civic ostracism excommunication under Halakha.

name: Karet
description: Serious excommunication; the dead under it become dybbukim.

name: Dybbukim
description: Spirits cut off from heaven that possess the living.

name: Radhanites
description: Jewish merchants from southern Iraq who trade widely, including in slaves.

name: Frederick II
description: Ruler under whom Jews held a silk monopoly in Sicily.

name: Lamed Vav Tzadikim Nistarim
description: The 36 hidden righteous souls in each generation who sustain the world.

name: Yeshivah shel Malah
description: Celestial level 5 regio where the dead study the True Torah under Zagzagel.

name: Zagzagel
description: Angel who presides over the Yeshivah shel Malah.

name: Ibbur
description: Spirit that co-inhabits a body to express its wisdom.

name: Rav Hamnuna Sava
description: Talmudic sage turned faerie appearing as an ass-driver teaching secrets of the Oral Torah.

name: Evil Eye
description: Harm from ill-will actually perpetrated by demons; also a Minor Supernatural Flaw.

name: Traditional Ward
description: Faerie Flaw representing observance of folk charms.

name: Vulnerable to Folk Tradition
description: Minor Hermetic Flaw letting targets gain resistance through folk rituals against the magus's magic.

name: Magic Lore
description: Ability determining resistance granted by folk charms.

name: City of Luz
description: Divine city of immortality reached via an almond tree in the Holy Land; level 3 and 7 regio.

name: Angel of Death
description: Angel unable to enter the City of Luz.

name: Celestial Regio
description: Places where the Divine touches Earth.

name: Dominion
description: The Divine realm whose auras rabbis may temper.

name: Educated (Hebrew)
description: Minor General Virtue granting 50 xp in Hebrew, Aramaic, Theology: Judaism and Judaic Lore.

name: Rosh Beth Din
description: Major Social Status Virtue for the head of the Beth Din court.

name: Kabbalist
description: Free Mythic Companion Social Status Virtue required of all kabbalists.

name: Shamash
description: Free Social Status Virtue for the servant of the synagogue.

name: Sofer
description: Free Social Status Virtue for the scribe of the Sefer Torah.

name: Astrological Magic
description: Minor Supernatural Virtue adding Artes Liberales to Kabbalah totals.

name: Philosophic Magic
description: Minor Supernatural Virtue adding Philosophiae to Kabbalah totals.

name: Karaite Magic
description: Major Hermetic Flaw listed for Jewish characters.

name: Gabai
description: Minor Social Status Flaw for Jewish characters.

name: Tzadik Nistar
description: Major Story Flaw for one of the hidden righteous.

name: Adjuration
description: Favored Ability of the Ba'al Shem.

name: Blessing
description: Favored Ability of the Ba'al Shem.

name: Intervention
description: Holy Power used to reach the City of Luz.

name: Purity
description: Holy Method replaceable by Merkavah.

name: Ignem
description: Form boosted by Asha Vahishta's Blessing.

name: Imaginem
description: Form boosted by Asha Vahishta's Blessing.

name: Vim
description: Form boosted by Khshathra Vairya's Blessing.

name: Aquam
description: Form boosted by Haurvatat's Blessing.

name: Auram
description: Form boosted by Haurvatat's Blessing.

name: Terram
description: Form boosted by Spenta Armaiti's Blessing.

name: Herbam
description: Form boosted by Ameretat's Blessing.

name: Animal
description: Form boosted by Vohu Manah's Blessing.

name: Corpus
description: Form boosted by Spenta Mainyu's Blessing.

name: Mentem
description: Form boosted by Spenta Mainyu's Blessing.
